 THIS W.P. IS FILED UNDER ARTICLE 226 OF THE CONSTITUTION OF INDIA PRAYING TO DIRECT THE R-2 TO CONSIDER THE REPRESENTATION OF THE PETITIONERS DATED 27.01.2018 VIDE ANNX-A AND THEREBY DIRECT THE R-2 TO PAY THE ENHANCED COMPENSATION AS PER THE PREVAILING MARKET RATE FOR THE LANDS SIMILARLY SITUATED ON THE SITE OF THE NATIONAL HIGHWAY NO.75.
AND ETC.,
 THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR PRELIMINARY HEARING IN 'B' GROUP, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

The Petitioners - land losers are ventilating the grievances in Writ jurisdiction as to non-consideration of their representation dated 27.01.2018, a copy whereof avails at Annexure-A wherein, they have sought for the enhancement of compensation both in respect of the lands comprised in the subject Sale Deeds, made over to the State and the other land that is now submerged.

Learned counsel for the Petitioners vehemently argues that the right to property having been constitutionally guaranteed under Article 300A, the State cannot take away, the private property without giving adequate compensation, notwithstanding what has been paid in terms of the Sale Deeds.

2. Learned counsel for the petitioners further argues that in respect of the submerged land, the compensation has to be determined normatively under Section 26 of the Right to Compensation Act,

3. After service of notice, the respondents nos. 1 & 2 have entered appearance through the learned AGA.

sentences.text: The Respondents Nos. 3 & 4 are represented by their Panel Counsel.

Both the advocates vehemently oppose the petition contending that once the consideration amount is accepted and Sale Deeds have been executed on 25.01.2018 & 28.02.2018, the land losers are only the sellers and therefore cannot seek anything in excess.

In respect of subsumed land, it is contended that they would instruct their clients to look into the grievance of the petitioners in accordance with law once the pending RTS proceedings are disposed off.
4. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and having perused the petition papers, this court is in complete agreement with the submission made on behalf of the Respondent.

Admittedly,
petitioners have sold the land by executing & registering two sale deeds in respect of particular lands after receiving the sale price as is reflected in Annexures-E & F.
Once price is paid for the sale transaction, it is not a case of compulsive acquisition under the 1894 Act.
Therefore, compensation or additional compensation cannot be sought for as a matter of right.
That being the position, the question of considering petitioners representation so far as the lands comprised in the sale deeds would not arise.
5. There is force in the submission of learned counsel for the petitioners that in respect of submerged land compensation has to be paid as provided under the provisions of Sec.26 of the 2013 Act.

However, the question of paying the compensation would arise only after and subject to outcome of the RTS proceedings pending on the file of jurisdictional Assistant Commissioner under the provisions of Sec.136(2) of the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964.

This having been said, the pendency of the said proceeding would not interdict the determination of the compensation amount, although its payment can be deferred, as rightly argued by counsel for the petitioners.

6. Petitioners are right in submitting that the compensation for the submerged land has to be determined without reference to the proceedings of the Deputy Commissioner held on 23.10.2017 unless there is evidentiary material to hold that petitioners too are signatories to the same.
However this is a matter in respect of which call has to be taken by the respondent- Deputy Commissioner and in this regard all contentions need to be kept open.

7. Petitioners counsel is also justified in insisting upon a direction to the Assistant Commissioner for the expeditious disposal of RTS proceedings so that the constitutional guarantee to the property rights is meaningful.
Therefore, the Assistant Commissioner should hear & dispose off the said proceedings within an outer limit of three months, in any circumstances.
On the basis of the outcome of the same, the decision to disburse the compensation to the owners of the land has to be taken within two months thereafter.
However in the meanwhile, the compensation shall be determined and put in a Court deposit.
